senses: Any set of machine-readable parallel bars or concentric circles, varying in width, spacing, or height, encoding information according to a symbology.

ety: From French ravelin, from Italian rivellino, of unclear origin: perhaps from Latin re- + vallum.

senses: One who violates (a rule, a boundary, another person's body, etc.); offender
ety: From Middle English violator, from Latin violātor. By surface analysis, violate + -or.
examples: The ordinance subjected any violator to a fine, to imprisonment for not more than six months, to community service, or to some combination of the three.

senses: Having the shape of a funnel.

ety: The noun is from Middle English swingel, from Old English swingel, swingelle (“whip, scourge”), equivalent to swing + -le. Related to Middle Dutch swingel, swengel, Dutch zwingel, zwengel. Doublet of swingel. The verb is from Middle English swingelen, from the noun. Related to Middle Dutch swingelen, swengelen.
